notes.text: Herod constructed an enormous expansion of this platform. Due to the precipitous drop of the Kidron Valley, Herod did not extend the platform to the east. He did, however, extend the platform in all other directions. When completed, it measured approximately 172,000square yards. The extensions to the south and west required the most effort because in these areas the hill's downward slope required the construction of massive retaining walls and a series of arches to support the platform. The retaining walls "towered more than 80feet above the roadways... and reached over 50feet below street level." It is generally thought that one of these corners is the pinnacle of the temple where the second temptation occurred (Matt. 4:5-7). [Traditionally, the southeast corner has been identified as the location for the second temptation. I believe the argument is stronger for the southwest corner. Since a possible focus of the second temptation was that of worldly recognition, the southwest corner makes better sense. An individual falling without harm from this corner would have been in full view of all the people in the busiest areas surrounding the temple platform, whereas the same event happening at the southeast corner would have been seen by a much smaller population.] (Richard Neitzel Holzapfel, Herodian Times and Historical Backgrounds, BYU Studies, vol. 36 (1996-97), Number 3--1996-97.)

notes.text: In this verse is an instance of that "parallelism" which is the peculiarity in the structure of Hebrew poetry, and consequently abounds in O. T. There are two principal varieties of it: (a) the second clause simply repeats, in different phraseology, the thought of the first; and (b) the second stands in contrast with the first. notes.text: Tzadi in Hebrew means the fish- hook With the tzadi one draws the fish out of the water. The word also has to do with hunting. The tzadij of Hasidism (the holy man or spiritual leader shows the way by his teaching and examples) is usual1y translated "a righteous man" - is actually one who catches fish, one who pulls men out of the water - which we understand as the time in which one is submerged. Pharaoh and Egypt were drowned in water; Moses, himself pulled out of water, became the (type for] the redeemer, pulling Israel out of the time spent in Egypt.
